title: Conveyancing Assistant / Conveyancing Legal Secretary

description:
Legal Administrator - Commercial Property Location: Stockton-on-Tees, Teesside
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Job Type: Permanent Full Time or Part Time
Working Hours: Flexible - Minimum 3 Days Per Week
Department: Commercial Property / Real Estate

An excellent opportunity has arisen for an experienced Legal Administrator / Legal Secretary to join the busy Commercial Property department of a well-established and highly regarded law firm in Stockton-on-Tees.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with previous legal secretarial or legal administration experience who enjoys providing high-quality support to fee earners within a busy and professional legal environment.

Working closely with the Commercial Property team, you'll provide essential administrative and secretarial support, assisting with a variety of commercial property transactions and helping to ensure matters progress smoothly and efficiently.

The firm offers a friendly, supportive working environment, with full-time or part-time hours considered (minimum 3 days per week), making this an attractive opportunity for someone seeking greater flexibility.

The Role As Legal Administrator, your responsibilities will include:
- Providing secretarial and administrative support to fee earners within the Commercial Property department.

- Preparing and issuing client bills and assisting with financial administration.
- Maintaining accurate electronic and paper files.
- Providing holiday and absence cover for other Legal Administrators.
- Supporting the wider team with general administration and office duties.

About You To be considered for this opportunity, you should have:
- Previous experience working as a Legal Secretary, Legal Administrator or Legal Assistant within a law firm.
- Strong audio typing and IT skills.
- Excellent organisational skills and the ability to prioritise a busy workload.
- Strong communication skills and a professional, client-focused approach.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- The ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- A positive, flexible attitude and the ability to thrive in a busy legal environment.

Previous Commercial Property, Real Estate or Conveyancing experience would be advantageous, although applications from candidates with experience in other areas of law are welcomed.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary depending on experience.
- Full-time or part-time working options (minimum 3 days per week).
- A supportive and welcoming legal team.
- The opportunity to work alongside experienced Commercial Property Solicitors.
- A varied and interesting role within an established law firm.
- A positive working environment where employees are valued and encouraged to develop.

title: Conveyancing Assistant
description:
Conveyancing Assistant/Resiential Property Assistant

Location: Whitley Bay, Tyne and Wear, North East England

Job Type: Permanent, Full-Time

Industry: Legal

Salary: £25,000 - £27,000 per annum

Job Description

The role of Conveyancing Assistant involves providing comprehensive administrative support to solicitors and conveyancers within a busy legal practise. The post holder assists with the progression of residential property transactions by managing documentation, liaising with clients and other parties, and ensuring compliance with legal protocols. This position requires strong organisational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work efficiently under supervision to meet deadlines.

Key Responsibilities
- Assist in the preparation and management of conveyancing documentation including contracts, deeds, and other legal forms.
- Liaise with clients, estate agents, mortgage lenders, surveyors, and local authorities to obtain necessary information and updates.
- Open and maintain client files, ensuring all records are accurate and up to date in accordance with firm procedures and regulatory requirements.
- Monitor the progress of property transactions and keep clients informed of developments in a timely and professional manner.
- Arrange and coordinate appointments, including property searches and exchanges of contracts, as directed by the conveyancer.
- Manage administrative tasks such as data entry, photocopying, scanning, and filing to support the conveyancing team.
- Ensure compliance with anti-money laundering regulations by assisting with due diligence checks and client identification processes.
- Support the conveyancers by preparing reports and correspondence as required.
- Maintain confidentiality and adhere to data protection legislation in all aspects of work.

The successful candidate will ideally have previous experience of LEAP.

The ideal candidate will be someone who who can work as part of a team and also on their own.

title: Graduate Paralegal - Housing Disrepair
description:
Paralegal - Housing Disrepair

We're recruiting a grad level / entry level Paralegal to join an established Housing Disrepair team in Newcastle.

This is a great opportunity for a law graduate looking to build proper hands-on experience in claimant work.

You won't be sitting on the sidelines watching other people run cases. You'll be involved in the early stages of claims, speaking with clients, reviewing case information and helping the wider team keep files moving. You'll have supervision and support, but you'll also need to be organised enough to manage a busy workload without being chased for everything.

The role

A large part of the job is making sure new and existing housing disrepair matters are dealt with properly and

efficiently. You'll speak with clients to gather the information needed to assess their claim, review incoming documentation and help determine which matters should progress.

You'll also work with triage information and assist with closing down cases that don't meet the required criteria. Once matters are underway, you'll help with the day-to-day administration and progression of files. That means dealing with correspondence, emails and calls, keeping the case management system accurate and liaising with surveyors, experts and other parties involved in the claim.

What we're looking for
- This role is aimed primarily at a law graduate who wants to develop practical experience within litigation.
- You'll need strong written and spoken communication skills because there is plenty of client contact.
- Some conversations will require patience and a clear explanation of what happens next, so good client care matters.
- Organisation is equally important. You'll be dealing with multiple files, competing deadlines and a steady flow of correspondence, so you need to be comfortable prioritising work and keeping accurate electronic records.
- Attention to detail is essential.
- You'll be reviewing information that can affect whether a claim progresses, and mistakes have consequences.
- You should also be comfortable handling confidential information, working as part of a wider legal team and asking questions when something needs clarification.

Package

Alongside a competitive salary, the business offers a broader benefits package including:
- Hybrid working for eligible roles
- annual leave plus bank holidays, increasing with service (option to purchase additional annual leave)
- Attendance-related bonus
- Funded quarterly team activities
- Workplace pension
- Death-in-service benefit after qualifying service
- Employee assistance programme with 24-hour support
- Cycle-to-work and public transport schemes
- Flu vaccination and eyecare support

Reasonable adjustments can be made throughout the recruitment process and, where required, within the role.
